questions.prompt: A floor card says $1/$2 NL, $100–$300 buy-in. What does that mean?

choices.text: Blinds are $1 and $2; you may buy in between $100 and $300.
The tournament starts at level 1 and ends at level 2.
You must buy in for exactly $200 every orbit.
The big blind doubles every 20 minutes.

questions.explanation: Cash stakes are fixed blinds plus a buy-in range, not a tournament clock.

questions.prompt: Which seat count is a full ring?
questions.explanation: Full ring is typically 8–9 handed. Six-handed is short-handed but not full ring.

questions.prompt: Effective stack is best described as…

choices.text: The largest stack at the table, always.
The smallest stack that can still contest the pot between the players involved.
The sum of every chip on the table.

questions.explanation: You cannot win more from an opponent than they have in front of them.

questions.prompt: Why does position matter more as stacks get deeper?

choices.text: Deeper stacks remove all postflop decisions.
The button must fold every hand when deep.
Blinds disappear once stacks exceed 100 big blinds.
More streets remain, so acting last gains more information.

questions.explanation: Deep cash play is multi-street. Acting last sees how others bet before you choose.
